1 Getting started

Opening the app

Use the web version at welltest.h2oil.co.uk, or the free iOS app. Both have every module, and every calculation runs on your device.

On the web the app works offline after the first visit. When a newer version is found, a bar offers Reload.

Your inputs stay in this browser’s storage, or in the iOS app on the device. Nothing is sent to a server: see Privacy (see Chapter 2.5).

The screen

  • Sidebar: nine groups. Select a group heading to open it; one group is open at a time. The search box 1 finds a page by name.
  • Hubs: one sidebar row, such as Chokes or Separators, stands for several pages. Tabs above the page switch between them.
  • Dashboard: search, favourites ★, recently used pages and a tile for every module (Dashboard (see Chapter 2.1)).
  • Well 2: the active well and the Well menu ⋯ (Several wells (see Chapter 1)).
  • File 3: New, Open…, Save and Save As… for project files (Saving work (see Chapter 1)).
  • Units 4: Imperial or Metric, the decimal comma 1,5 and the Std base conditions (Units (see Chapter 1)).
  • Quick Report 5: one PDF of every page you have run (Reports (see Chapter 1)).
  • Export buttons: Copy results, PDF, PNG, CSV and JSON for the page on screen.

Your first calculation

  1. Open Production & Reservoir in the sidebar and select Oil & Gas Rate.
  2. The page opens with example inputs: a 60 min interval, meter readings 1000 bbl (159 m³) and 1004.5 bbl (160 m³), 35 °API, separator 500 psig (3447 kPa(g)), 50 inH2O (124 mbar) on a 2 in (50.8 mm) plate.
  3. Select Calculate. Combined Results shows Oil Rate 97.7 BPD (15.5 m³/d), Gas Rate 3792.554 MSCFD (107392.993 m³/d) and GOR 38809 SCF/STB (6912 sm³/sm³) (the page writes the GOR unit as scf/bbl).
  4. Change an input and select Calculate again. Your inputs are saved as you type.
  5. Use the export buttons for a PDF of the page, or Copy results for the text.

In Metric mode the page shows the same values converted; the calculation is the same.

Saving work

  • Autosave: each page keeps its inputs on this device as you type. The header shows Autosave on, then the time of the last save.
  • Project files (.h2oilproj): File → Save puts every page’s inputs, Client & Well Info, every well, the PRiSM data and the report snapshots in one file. Open… loads it on any device with the app. Save As… writes a copy under a new name.
  • File → New clears every page for a new job. It keeps your device settings and the Report Prepared By fields.
  • Device settings are not in project files: the units system, the decimal comma, favourites and the open sidebar group.

Fill in Client & Well Info (see Chapter 2.3) first: its details go on every report.

Several wells

A project can hold several wells. Each well keeps its own inputs and results; every page shows the active well.

  • Well menu (⋯ next to the well name): New well…, Duplicate this well…, Rename…, Delete this well….
  • Copy this page’s inputs from: copies the page on screen from another well.
  • Compare wells opens Well Comparison (see Chapter 2.4).
  • Share read-only snapshot: This page, Job report (this well) or All wells comparison, as a read-only HTML file.

A project always has at least one well. Deleting a well cannot be undone unless you saved a project file.

Units and base conditions

Every calculation runs in oilfield (imperial) units. Metric converts what you type and what you read; Imperial goes back. Labels change with the setting, so the guides quote labels without their unit.

  • Std sets the base (standard) conditions for gas volumes. “calc default” keeps each page’s own basis; the other choices are 60 °F at 14.696, 14.65 or 14.73 psia, and 15 °C or 0 °C at 101.325 kPa.
  • 1,5 turns on the decimal comma: 12,5 typed in a number field is read as 12.5. While it is on, 1,500 means 1.5.
  • PRiSM works in oilfield units only, and says so at the top of the page in Metric mode.

Reports

  • Export buttons on each calculator page: Copy results (text; tables tab-separated), PDF, PNG (charts), CSV and JSON of the inputs and results.
  • The PDF opens a print-ready page; use your browser’s print to save it as a PDF file.
  • Quick Report: one PDF of every page you have calculated. Its ▾ picks a template: All captured pages, Daily well-test report, Final well-test report, or your own (New template).
  • The client logo is used only when it is ticked in Client & Well Info (see Chapter 2.3).

Jobs that use several pages

How do I… (see Chapter 1) lists common jobs step by step, with what to carry from one page to the next.

Live data in one page

Connect the gauges in Modbus Configuration (see Chapter 6.2), watch them in Mini WellOS (see Chapter 6.1), keep and export the history in Historian (see Chapter 6.3), then load the exported series in PRiSM — Well Test Analysis (see Chapter 5.1) (the steps (see Chapter 1)).

Troubleshooting

  • A page keeps odd values: there is no reset for one page. Change the values back, or use File → New for a clean job (save a project file first). A new well (Well menu → New well…) also starts with empty pages; delete it afterwards if you only needed a clean page.
  • Clearing site data in your browser’s site settings removes everything the app stored on this device. Save a project file first.
  • The 3D view stays blank: it needs graphics support and, on the web, downloads its engine on first use. Use the 2D view.
  • Opening a file on iOS: save the file in the Files app first, then pick it there.
  • Where your data is: in this browser’s storage on this device (Privacy (see Chapter 2.5)); project files and exports go where you save them.
  • Contact: software@h2oil.co.uk.

More answers: Troubleshooting and FAQ (see Appendix D).

How do I…

Design a well test spread

Size the surface spread for the expected rates.

  1. Client & Well Info (see Chapter 2.3): Client, well and rig.
  2. Well Test Simulator (see Chapter 11.1): Enter the rates, pressures and bean; read velocities and hydrate margins. Carry: gas, oil and water rates; wellhead pressure; separator pressure
  3. Dual Choke (see Chapter 3.3): Check the bean and critical flow. Carry: bean size
  4. Separator Retention (see Chapter 8.1): Retention time at the test rates. Carry: separator size
  5. Flare Simulation (see Chapter 9.1): Radiation at the burner for the gas rate. Carry: flare radiation
  6. PRV / Relief Sizing (see Chapter 9.4): Relief load and orifice. Carry: relief load
  7. Quick Report ▾ → Final well-test report.

Clean up and unload the cushion

Unload the completion fluid to the burner, then go through the separator.

  1. Well Test Simulator (see Chapter 11.1): Follow field scenario FS-1 (see Chapter 12): it sets the simulator up for an unload to the burner. Carry: unload rate and gas rate
  2. Flare Simulation (see Chapter 9.1): Radiation at the burner for that gas rate. Carry: burner back pressure
  3. SO2 / H2S Dispersion Screening (see Chapter 9.3): Where the burner gas and the hydrogen sulphide (H2S) in it go downwind.
  4. Hydrate Management (see Chapter 7.3): Hydrate risk downstream of the choke. Carry: choke outlet pressure and temperature
  5. Chemical Injection (see Chapter 7.4): Inhibitor rate and pump setting, if needed.

Meter gas

Pick the plate, measure the rate and check the meters.

  1. Orifice Plate Selection (see Chapter 3.2): The plate that keeps the differential pressure (DP) inside the transmitter range. Carry: plate bore and DP range
  2. AGA-3 Gas Metering (see Chapter 3.1): Gas rate from the readings. Carry: gas rate
  3. Meter Proving & Net Standard Volume (see Chapter 3.9): Liquid meter factor from the prover runs. Carry: meter factor
  4. Separator Sampling & GOR QC (see Chapter 3.10): Separator GOR and sample checks.

Prepare the daily report

One PDF for the day.

  1. Well Comparison (see Chapter 2.4): Make sure the right well is active.
  2. Client & Well Info (see Chapter 2.3): Check the header details and select Save Information.
  3. Calculate the day’s pages: each calculation is captured for the report. Carry: snapshots
  4. Quick Report ▾ → Daily well-test report.

Check hydrate risk at the choke

Find the cold point and protect it.

  1. Well Test Simulator (see Chapter 11.1): Choke outlet pressure and temperature (or Dual Choke (see Chapter 3.3)). Carry: choke outlet P and T
  2. Hydrate Management (see Chapter 7.3): Hydrate margin per segment and inhibitor rate. Carry: hydrate margin
  3. Chemical Injection (see Chapter 7.4): Pump and injection point for the inhibitor. Carry: inhibitor rate

Interpret a build-up

Get permeability k, skin and the extrapolated pressure p* from a shut-in.

  1. Build-up Surveillance (see Chapter 5.7): Find and interpret the shut-ins in gauge data. Carry: rate history; producing time
  2. PRiSM — Well Test Analysis (see Chapter 5.1): Or step by step: Data, Flow periods, Diagnose, Model & fit, Report. Carry: k, skin, p*

Analyse a DFIT

Closure, leak-off and p_i.

  1. PRiSM — Well Test Analysis (see Chapter 5.1): Test DFIT, load the record, datum TVD and wellbore, ▶ Analyse DFIT, steps 2 to 5 (DFIT mode (see Chapter 5.1)). Carry: closure gradient, p_i, k

Check whether a DFIT is interpretable

Before trusting the numbers.

  1. PRiSM — Well Test Analysis (see Chapter 5.1): Test triage on step 1: checks, blunder cards, re-pump verdict, grade. Carry: grade A–D

Size a flowline or check erosion

Pressure drop, velocity and sand erosion.

  1. Multiphase Flowline Pressure Drop (see Chapter 4.3): Pressure drop and velocities along the line. Carry: rates; velocities
  2. Pipe Sizing (see Chapter 4.5): Pipe size for the velocity limits. Carry: velocity against the API RP 14E limit
  3. Pipe Service Life (see Chapter 7.6): Sand erosion time per segment.

Plan a well kill

Kill fluid and volumes.

  1. Well Kill & Bullhead (see Chapter 7.8): Kill weight and bullhead volumes. Carry: kill weight; volumes
  2. Cement & Completion Fluids (see Chapter 7.9): Brine blend for that weight; cement slurry volumes if needed.

Live data from a gauge

From the gauge to an interpretation.

  1. Modbus Configuration (see Chapter 6.2): Connect the device and set up the tags. Carry: tags
  2. Mini WellOS (see Chapter 6.1): Watch the live values and alarms.
  3. Historian (see Chapter 6.3): Keep the history and export it. Carry: exported series
  4. PRiSM — Well Test Analysis (see Chapter 5.1): Load the series and interpret it.

Gas properties for a calculation

Z and related properties at line conditions.

  1. Gas PVT (see Chapter 10.3): Z, k, viscosity and J-T coefficient at the line pressure and temperature. Carry: Z, k, J-T coefficient
  2. Enter them on the page that needs them.

2 Overview

2.1 Dashboard

The start page: search every calculator, pin favourites and open any module from its tile.

What it does

Tiles sit under the sidebar group headings. Each has a group badge and one line on what the module does.

When to use it

  • To find a calculator by name, method or standard.
  • To get back to the pages you use most.

Step by step

  1. Select Dashboard in Overview.
  2. Type in the search box 1: a name, a method or a standard. Tiles that do not match are hidden.
  3. Select ☆ on a tile to pin it to the favourites row 2. Select ★ to unpin it.
  4. Select a tile 3 to open its module. The pages you open are listed under Recently used.

Inputs

InputDefaultWhat to enter
Search calculatorsWords in a tile title, description or group.

Results and verdicts

ResultMeaning
FavouritesYour pinned tiles.
Recently usedThe last pages you opened.

  • The ⚠ on the ESD Hi-Pilot tile is its icon, not a warning.

Pitfalls

2.2 Help & User Guide

A guide for every module, with search, "How do I…" tasks, the simulator course and field scenarios.

What it does

Every guide has the same sections: what it does, when to use it, steps, inputs, results and verdicts, an example, tips and standards.

Help is never put in reports, autosave or project files.

When to use it

  • You are new to a page, or a verdict is not clear.
  • A job needs several modules in order.

Step by step

  1. Select Help & Guide in Overview. On other pages, the ? next to the page title opens that page’s guide.
  2. Type in the search box 1: a module, a label, a standard or an oilfield term. Select a result to open it at that section.
  3. Or pick a module in Contents 2, or a job under How do I….
  4. Select Getting started 3 for a tour of the app.
  5. In a guide, Open this page → goes to the module. Back returns to the page you came from.
  6. To print, pick a scope in the Print menu; Images off prints text only.

Results and verdicts

3 Metering & Chokes

3.1 AGA-3 Gas Metering

Gas rate through an orifice meter from the differential, static pressure and temperature (AGA Report No. 3).

What it does

Cd, Y1 and Z, then the rate at your base conditions. To choose a plate, use Orifice Plate Selection (see Chapter 3.2).

When to use it

  • Each orifice reading.
  • Checking a flow computer.

Step by step

  1. Select AGA-3 Gas Metering in Metering & Chokes.
  2. Enter the Pipe Internal Dia 1 and the Orifice Diameter of the plate in use.
  3. Enter the Diff Pressure 2, Static Pressure and Flowing Temp.
  4. Enter the gas gravity and the CO2, H2S and N2 content.
  5. Select Calculate Gas Rate. Read the rate in Flow Results 3.
  6. To send the rate to PRiSM, enter the step start, then select Append rate step to PRiSM.

Flowing Temp80 °F (26.7 °C)
Gas Specific Gravity0.65
Gas gravity basisReal
CO20.5 %
H2S0 %
N21 %
Z-factor overrideBlank: built-in DAK Z.
Use calculated ZZ from Gas PVT.

Step start, hours on the PRiSM data clock

Worked example

The default inputs

  • 2 in (50.8 mm) plate in a 4.026 in (102 mm) run, 50 inH2O (124 mbar), 500 psig (3447 kPa(g)), 80 °F (26.7 °C).

Result:

  • 4122.5 MSCFD (116736.0 m³/d); β 0.4968, Cd 0.6031, Y1 0.99884, Z 0.9153.

In Metric mode the page shows the same values converted; the calculation is the same.

Tips and pitfalls

Pitfalls

  • A typed Z stays in use until you clear it. The Notes then show a ⚠.

Standards and references

  • AGA Report No. 3 / API MPMS Ch. 14.3 — orifice flow equation

Related modules

Orifice Plate Selection (see Chapter 3.2) · Gas PVT (see Chapter 10.3) · Separator Sampling & GOR QC (see Chapter 3.10)

3.2 Orifice Plate Selection

Picks the orifice bore that keeps the differential inside your window of the transmitter range at a target gas rate.

What it does

The page runs the AGA-3 Gas Metering (see Chapter 3.1) calculation backwards. It finds the exact bore for your design differential, then the nearest 0.125" plate that stays inside your low and high limits.

When to use it

  • Before a test: choose the plate for the expected gas rate.
  • During a test: the differential nears the top or bottom of the range.

Step by step

  1. Select Orifice Plate Selection in Metering & Chokes.
  2. Enter the Target gas rate 1 and the meter run, line and gas data.
  3. Enter the Transmitter range, 0 to of your DP cell.
  4. Set the window: Low limit, High limit and Design differential.
  5. Select Select Plate. The page also updates on every change.
  6. Read the verdict, then the Orifice bore 2.
  7. Plan plate changes with the Plate-Change Points table 3.

Inputs

InputDefaultWhat to enter
Target gas rate5000 MSCFD (141584 m³/d)At the base conditions.
Meter run internal diameter4.026 in (102 mm)Measured bore; at least 2 in (50.8 mm).
Static (line) pressure500 psig (3447 kPa(g))
Flowing temperature80 °F (26.7 °C)
Gas specific gravity0.65
Gas gravity basisReal
CO20.5 %
N21.0 %Not in the Z correction.
H2S0 %
Transmitter range, 0 to200 inH2O (498 mbar)DP cell upper range value.
Low limit20 %
High limit80 %
Design differential50 %Where the target rate should sit.
Base temperature60 °F (15.6 °C)Follows the header Std setting.
Base pressure, absolute14.696 psia (101 kPa)

Results and verdicts

ResultMeaning
Orifice bore, Beta ratioThe plate to fit and d/D (AGA-3: 0.10 to 0.75).
Exact Bore & NeighboursNext plates up and down.
Plate-Change PointsRate at the low and high % of range.
  • ✓ The plate reads inside the window. Fit it; confirm the bore on site.
  • ✗ No 0.125" plate fits the window. Widen it or change the range.
  • ✗ Too much gas: use a larger run or a higher range.
  • ✗ Too little gas: use a smaller run or a lower range.
  • ⚠ x1 above 0.2: Y1 is outside its validated range.
  • ⚠ Line pressure is low for this range.
  • ⚠ Run below 2 in (50.8 mm): an estimate only.
  • ⚠ β above 0.6: check the upstream straight lengths.

Worked example

The default inputs

  • 5000 MSCFD (141584 m³/d), 4.026 in (102 mm) run, 500 psig (3447 kPa(g)), 80 °F (26.7 °C), gravity 0.65, cell 0 to 200 inH2O (498 mbar).

Result:

  • ✓ 1.875 in (47.625 mm) plate, β 0.466, 97.2 inH2O (241.9 mbar) = 48.6 % of range.
  • Change down below 3214 MSCFD (91010 m³/d), up above 6406 MSCFD (181397 m³/d).

In Metric mode the page shows the same values converted; the calculation is the same.

Tips and pitfalls

Tips

  • Keep the next plate up and down at the meter.

Pitfalls

  • Enter the measured tube bore (4.026 in (102 mm)), not the nominal size.

Standards and references

  • AGA Report No. 3 / API MPMS Ch. 14.3 — β limits
  • ISO 5167-1 and -2 — DP range

Related modules

AGA-3 Gas Metering (see Chapter 3.1) · Meter Proving & Net Standard Volume (see Chapter 3.9) · Separator Sampling & GOR QC (see Chapter 3.10)

Reviewed for v3.3.2

3.3 Dual Choke

Two chokes in series: intermediate pressure, drop on each, critical checks, equivalent bean (see Appendix B) and rate.

What it does

Gas: the API 14B equation on both beans. Multiphase: Gilbert through the equivalent bean.

When to use it

  • A fixed and an adjustable choke in series.
  • Which choke takes the drop.

Step by step

  1. Select Chokes in Metering & Chokes, then Dual Choke.
  2. Enter the Upstream Pressure 1 and Downstream Pressure 2.
  3. Choose the Fluid Type.
  4. Enter each choke size in 64ths and its Cd.
  5. For multiphase, also enter the oil gravity, GOR (see Appendix B) and Water Cut.
  6. Select Calculate. Read P2 3, the drop on each choke and the critical checks.

InputDefaultWhat to enter

Downstream Pressure500 psig (3447 kPa(g))
Fluid TypeGas Only
Flowing Temp150 °F (65.6 °C)
Choke 1 Size32Upstream choke, 64ths.
Choke 1 Cd0.85
Choke 2 Size24
Choke 2 Cd0.85
Gas Specific Gravity0.65
Oil Gravity35 °API
GOR800 SCF/STB (142 sm³/sm³)

Results and verdicts

ResultMeaning
Intermediate Pressure (P2)Between the chokes.
Flow EstimateGas rate, or Gilbert rates.

Worked example

The default inputs (gas)

  • 1500 psig (10342 kPa(g)) to 500 psig (3447 kPa(g)), 32/64 then 24/64.

Result:

  • P2 1400.7 psig (9657.5 kPa(g)); the 24/64 choke takes 90 % and flows critical.
  • Equivalent bean 22.4/64; 4146.7 MSCFD (117421.3 m³/d).

In Metric mode the page shows the same values converted; the calculation is the same.

Tips and pitfalls

Pitfalls

  • Pressures are gauge. The multiphase rate assumes critical flow.

Standards and references

  • Gilbert (1954) — bean correlation

4.3 Multiphase Flowline Pressure Drop

Multiphase pressure drop from the choke outlet to the separator and from the gas PCV to the flare tip, with choke and PCV checks.

What it does

Both lines are marched back: from the separator pressure to the choke outlet, and from the flare tip to the PCV outlet.

When to use it

  • Is the line big enough? Does the choke stay critical?
  • Flare line: Mach, PSV (see Appendix B) back-pressure, cold gas after the PCV.

Step by step

  1. Select Flowline Pressure Drop in Well Test & Flowlines.
  2. Fill Stream & Conditions 1, with the WHP (see Appendix B).
  3. Choose the Temperature model. Coupled: fill Heat Loss (coupled temperature model only).
  4. Fill Segments: Choke Outlet to Separator: length, inside diameter, elevation change.
  5. Fill the flare data and Segments: Gas PCV Outlet to Flare Tip.
  6. Read Line Summary 2 and Gas PCV and Flare Line.

Results and verdicts

ResultMeaning
Required pressure downstream of the chokeP2; critical at p2/p1 ≤ 0.588 with liquid; for dry gas the ratio comes from k (the page shows the value used). Then the PCV outlet back-pressure.
Segment tablesPattern, holdup, pressure, velocity, Mach, ρv².
  • ✓ Choke critical: the rate does not depend on the separator.
  • ⚠ A separator pressure change changes the rate.
  • ✗ WHP below P2: lower the separator pressure or enlarge the line.
  • ✗ Critical velocity in the line: enlarge it.
  • ✓ The line pressure drop.
  • ⚠ Above the erosional velocity: larger line or lower rate.
  • ✓ PCV drop; if choked, check sizing and noise.
  • ⚠ The PCV is nearly wide open.
  • ✗ Back-pressure at or above the separator pressure.
  • ✓ Flare line Mach is fine.
  • ⚠ Mach above 0.5 or high ρv²: noise and vibration.
  • ✗ Mach above 0.7 or a choked flare line: enlarge it.
  • ⚠ Heat the gas or inject inhibitor.
  • ⚠ Check the materials.
  • ✓ Back-pressure within 10 % of the PSV set pressure.
  • ⚠ Use a balanced-bellows or pilot PSV, or a larger line.
  • ⚠ PSV set pressure not above the separator, or within 10 % of it: check.
  • ⚠ Gas rate is zero.

4.4 Line Heat Loss & Arrival Temperature

Temperature along bare, insulated or buried lines, with J-T cooling at chokes, arrival temperature and a hydrate check.

What it does

Each segment loses heat to air or soil. A choke drop at a segment inlet cools the whole stream. Each segment is checked against the hydrate temperature at its coldest point.

  5. Select Calculate. Read the verdict 2 and Segment Temperatures.

Segment TemperaturesJ-T drop, UA, arrival temperature, heat lost, hydrate temperature, margin.
  • ✓ At least 5 °F (2.78 °C) above the hydrate temperature.
  • ⚠ Under 5 °F (2.78 °C) margin: plan heat or inhibitor.
  • ✗ Hydrates can form: heat the stream or inject inhibitor.
  • ⚠ Check on Hydrate Management (see Chapter 7.3).

Worked example

The defaults, 40 °F (4.44 °C) air

  • 5 MMSCFD (142 10³ m³/d), 2500 psig (17237 kPa(g)) and 150 °F (65.6 °C) in; 1500 psi (10342 kPa) choke drop at segment 2.

Result:

  • After the choke 42.3 °F (5.7 °C), arrival 42.1 °F (5.6 °C): ✗.
  • Inlet temperature 182 °F (83.3 °C) (a heater upstream) gives ✓.

In Metric mode the page shows the same values converted; the calculation is the same.

Tips and pitfalls

Tips

  • Put each choke drop on the segment that starts at the choke.

Pitfalls

  • Pressure ignores line friction: use Multiphase Flowline Pressure Drop (see Chapter 4.3).

Standards and references

Standard heat-transfer relations (page Notes).

Related modules

Multiphase Flowline Pressure Drop (see Chapter 4.3) · Hydrate Management (see Chapter 7.3) · Indirect Heater (see Chapter 8.4) · Chemical Injection (see Chapter 7.4)

5 Production & Reservoir

5.1 PRiSM — Well Test Analysis

PRiSM works in oilfield units (psia, hours, STB/d or Mscf/d, md, ft, cp, 1/psi). The Metric setting does not convert PRiSM inputs or results — enter and read values in these units.

Interprets a pressure test: load the data, pick the period, read the derivative, fit a model, report k, skin (see Appendix B) and storage.

What it does

Five steps, 1 Data to 5 Report, in the step bar.

The results rail shows the latest fit and straight line. Tools holds the specialist panels.

When to use it

  • After a build-up, drawdown, injection or fall-off test.
  • To check for damage before or after a stimulation.
  • With rate-only data, for decline analysis and EUR.
  • After a DFIT (see Appendix B) (DFIT mode (see Chapter 5.1)).

Step by step

  1. Select PRiSM — Well Test Analysis in Production & Reservoir.
  2. Select Try demo data 1 or Load data.
  3. Fill in Well & Test: test type, rate, h, φ, B, μ, ct and rw.
  4. Select ▶ Analyse 2: PRiSM picks the period, fits a model, fills the rail 3.
  5. Check each step with the step bar 4: Flow periods (see Chapter 5.1), Diagnose (see Chapter 5.1), Model & fit (see Chapter 5.1).
  6. Open Report (5) to export the results.

Results and verdicts

ResultMeaning
k, khPermeability (md), flow capacity (md·ft), 95 % range.
Skin SPositive: damage; negative: stimulation. With Δp_skin, FE and DR.
C, C_DWellbore storage (bbl/psi) and C_D.
r_invHow far the test saw.
Straight lineSemilog m, k and S (MDH, Horner or superposition): checks the model.
  • ✓ Step-bar tick: the step has what it needs.

Worked example

The demo drawdown

  • Try demo data (55 points, 850 STB/d, pi 4,200 psia, h 35 ft), then ▶ Analyse.

Result:

  • Homogeneous, ✓ converged, R² 1.00000: k 45.0 md, S +2.50, C 8.47e-4 bbl/psi, r_inv 1,549 ft.
  • Straight line (MDH): m 121 psi/cycle, k 45.0 md, S +2.49, FE 0.76.

Tips and pitfalls

Tips

  • Run ▶ Analyse, then refine the period, window and model.
  • If line and model differ by over 5 % in k, check the IARF (see Appendix B) window.

Pitfalls

  • A field marked sample holds a demo value: enter yours.

Standards and references

  • Bourdet (1989, 2002) — derivative and models
  • Agarwal, Al-Hussainy and Ramey (1970) — storage and skin
  • Horner (1951) — semilog lines

Related modules

Build-up Surveillance (see Chapter 5.7) · Oil Well IPR (see Chapter 5.5) · Gas Deliverability & AOF (see Chapter 5.4) · Historian (see Chapter 6.3)

1 Data

What it does

Load the record, check how it was read, enter the well and fluid.

Step by step
  1. Select Load data (file or paste) or Try demo data.
  2. Check Column Mapping and Units, then Apply mapping.
  3. Drop bad points with Cleanup or Crop & trim the record.
  4. Fill Well & Test; Estimate from PVT… gives B, μ, ct.
  5. Fill the Gauge register and the Sequence of events.
Inputs
InputDefaultWhat to enter
Test typeDrawdown (demo)Or Buildup, Injection, Falloff, Auto-detect.
Rate qSTB/d or Mscf/d; can come from the data.
h, φ, rw, B, μ, ctft, fraction, ft, RB/STB, cp, 1/psi.
pi, tp, shut-in time, pwf at shut-inBuild-ups: from the data if blank.
Try demo data
Load dataFile or pasted text.
Apply mapping
Confirm crop
Gauge registerSerial, type, range, resolution, accuracy, calibration, depth.
Sequence of eventsOpens, shut-ins, rate changes, notes.

2 Flow periods

What it does

One band per flow period; the selected one is analysed.

Step by step
  1. Pick a period band or row.
  2. Select Use all data to clear it, or Crop data… to trim.
  3. Leave t_p blank to use the rate history.
Tips and pitfalls

Tips

  • After several rates, enter them in Multi-Rate History (optional) on step 1.

3 Diagnose

What it does

Δp and the Bourdet derivative. Flat: radial flow (IARF). Unit slope: storage. Half slope: linear flow.

Step by step
  1. Choose the plot in Plot: log-log, MDH, Horner, history and more.
  2. In Straight-line analysis & skin, run the line and read k, S, Δp_skin and FE.
  3. Line tools pick a plateau, slope or boundary.
Results and verdicts
  • ✓ Derivative-plateau check: the line and the derivative level agree.
  • ⚠ No unit-slope points: C is not determined from the data.

4 Model & fit

What it does

Model (46 models), Parameters, Type-curve match and Regression (fit with 95 % ranges).

Step by step
  1. In Model library select Find best models, or pick one.
  2. Set start values in Parameters; fix what you know.
  3. Select Run regression; read R², ΔAIC and the Skin check card.
Results and verdicts
  • ✓ converged: the fit settled.
Tips and pitfalls

Tips

  • Prefer the simplest model; ΔAIC below about 2 does not separate two.

5 Report

What it does

Summary, results with source and 95 % range, plots, skin check.

Step by step
  1. Fit a model on step 4 first.
  2. Select Export PDF, or export CSV or XML.
  3. Client and well names come from Client & Well Info (see Chapter 2.3).

Tools drawer

What it does

PVT, tide, datasets, deconvolution, gas m(p), deliverability, rate-transient, plot tools, decline, saved fits.

Step by step
  1. Select Tools, then a panel; it opens on its own step.
  2. Use deconvolution for multi-rate data.
  3. Save and compare fits in the fit workspace.

DFIT mode

What it does

Fracture injection falloff: ISIP (see Appendix B), closure (see Appendix B), net pressure (see Appendix B), fluid efficiency (see Appendix B), leak-off, p_i and k. Field units only.

Step by step
  1. Select Test DFIT (fracture injection).
  2. Load demo DFIT fills the well and analyses at once. Or load your record (rate in bbl/min), enter the datum TVD and wellbore, tick psig channels and select ▶ Analyse DFIT.
  3. Read the triage checks, re-pump verdict and grade A–D (provisional).
  4. A blunder card: Apply fix or It is real (logged).
Worked example

Reference demo

Result:

  • ISIP 7,599 psia; closure 7,003 psia (0.700 psi/ft, high, provisional); pn 596 psi; η 0.898; p_i 4,496 psia [4,491–4,721] (medium, provisional); grade B, provisional.
Standards and references
  • Nolte (1979), SPE 8341
  • Barree, Barree and Craig (2009), SPE 107877
  • Nolte, Maniere and Owens (1997), SPE 38676

DFIT 2 ISIP & friction, 3 Pre-closure

What it does

ISIP from wave, falloff and step-down. Closure from every method, in families (see Appendix B) F0–F4: one value within τ, else a range with both ends carried. Labels: provisional, not calibrated.

Step by step
  1. Read the closure board: strip, label, methods, Why, stability.
  2. A pick under the frictional limit is vetoed.
  3. Override with Use another value and a reason.
  4. Read the provisional leak-off type (PDL (see Appendix B)…), η, pn, R_vis (see Appendix B), CL, geometry, what-if.

DFIT 4 After closure & model

What it does

After-closure (see Appendix B) p_i with bracket; kh/μ or k bounds; leak check.

Step by step
  1. Set the origin; read the log-log, F_L, F_R and impulse (see Appendix B) plots.
  2. Tab Leak-off model: Simulate in the sandbox, or History match, Fit.
  3. Tab Uncertainty: P10/P50/P90 of each output.
  4. Tab What this test can tell (after a fit).

DFIT 5 Report, Tools

What it does

PDF, picks, frac-design CSV; a Quick Report key line; Well Comparison (see Chapter 2.4) shows the closure gradient.

Step by step
  1. Open in PTA (transient) hands over p_i only if labelled high or medium; with a closure range pick the F1 or F2 chain.
  2. Tools: designer, sandbox, replay, water hammer, notes. Radial flow often needs far more shut-in than allowed: plan for p_i and k bounds.
  3. Spurt is not separable: η is an upper bound.

Reviewed for v3.4.1

5.4 Gas Deliverability & AOF

AOF and deliverability of a gas well from test points, by C and n and by LIT.

What it does

Fits q = C (p̄r² − pwf²)ⁿ and p̄r² − pwf² = a·q + b·q² to the points, then tabulates both curves.

When to use it

  • After a flow-after-flow, isochronal or modified isochronal test.
  • For a single-point AOF with an assumed n.

Step by step

  1. Select Gas Deliverability & AOF in Production & Reservoir.
  2. Pick the Test type 1; enter p̄r and the AOF back-pressure.
  3. Fill Test Points 2 (or Insert example, or paste and Import rows).
  4. Select Calculate; read the verdict and both equations 3.
  5. Read the Deliverability Table.

Inputs

InputDefaultWhat to enter

Average reservoir pressure, absolute1952 psi (13459 kPa)

Results and verdicts

ResultMeaning
Exponent n, Coefficient Cn from 0.5 (turbulent) to 1.0 (laminar).
a, b, Non-Darcy shareLIT terms.
AOFFrom each method.

5.7 Build-up Surveillance

Finds the shut-ins in permanent-gauge data, interprets each build-up and trends skin (see Appendix B), k, p* (see Appendix B) and PI.

What it does

Each build-up gets an IARF (see Appendix B) window, semilog line, model match, S_err and confidence label. Alerts flag a skin change.

Partial rate cuts are listed, not interpreted; Open this build-up in PRiSM to deconvolve.

When to use it

  • When new permanent-gauge data arrive.
  • To decide on a stimulation from the skin trend.

Step by step

6 Live Data

6.1 Mini WellOS

A live control-room view of the spread: tiles, process view, trends, alarms, a CSV log and a pressure trend for PRiSM.

What it does

Form data runs the simulator model from the Well Test Simulator (see Chapter 11.1) inputs or the sample well. Modbus data shows the tags linked on the Modbus Configuration (see Chapter 6.2) page, each with a quality mark. The Historian (see Chapter 6.3) records every value.

When to use it

  • Watch a live test from the gauges and the PLC, all alarms in one list.
  • Train a crew on the simulator model before any hardware is connected.
  • Send a gauge pressure trend to PRiSM.

Step by step

  1. Select Mini WellOS in Live Data.
  2. Choose the data source 1: Form data or Modbus data.
  3. In Modbus data with no tags linked, select Use the Modbus simulator demo in the banner (virtual slave).
  4. In Form data, set the speed 2: 1×, 10× or 60×. In Modbus data that place holds Pause polling.
  5. Switch the process view with 3D or 2D 3; without 3D the page shows 2D.
  6. Read the tiles and Live variables: each value shows its quality and source.
  7. Under Trends, tick up to six variables; pick the window, 5 min to 12 h.
  8. Under Alarms: Ack or Acknowledge all; Events keeps the history.
  9. Under CSV logging: Start logging, then Download CSV.
  10. Under Send to PRiSM, choose the Pressure gauge (WHP (see Appendix B) by default) and select Send trend window to PRiSM.

6.2 Modbus Configuration

Each tag reads in its own units; a linked tag is converted to field units (psig, °F, MMSCFD, bbl/d). Metric mode does not change this page.

Connects PLCs, RTUs and gauges over Modbus TCP or RTU, scales registers into tags and links them to app variables.

What it does

Add the devices, then one tag per register. A linked tag feeds Mini WellOS (see Chapter 6.1); the Historian (see Chapter 6.3) records it. The page is read-only unless writes are enabled.

When to use it

  • Before a test: map the gauge or PLC registers.
  • Training with no hardware: load the simulator.
  • A value reads wrong: check table, address, type and word order.

Step by step

  1. Select Modbus Config in Live Data.
  2. No hardware? Select Load simulator demo 1: 37 tags on the virtual slave.
  3. Otherwise select + Add device, one row per device (Devices (see Chapter 6.2)).
  4. Select + Add tag for each register and link it (Tags (see Chapter 6.2)).
  5. Select Test at the end of the device row 2; Status shows the result. Test read checks one tag.
  6. Select Start live monitor to poll; Pause polling stops it for every page.
  7. Read the Configuration summary 3: the issues are listed under it; a highlighted row has the reason as a tooltip.
  8. Open Mini WellOS (see Chapter 6.1) and set its data source to Modbus data.

  • ⚠ Fix the highlighted rows.
  • ✓ The demo replaced the configuration.

6.3 Historian

Values keep the unit they were recorded in; Metric mode does not convert them.

Records, trends, tabulates and exports tag data from Modbus, Mini WellOS and the Well Test form, on this device.

What it does

It records the Modbus Configuration (see Chapter 6.2) tags, the Mini WellOS (see Chapter 6.1) form values, and the Well Test form while Log form data is ticked. Times are UTC, shown in local time.

When to use it

  • Review a test, tag by tag, over hours or days.
  • Export data for a report or PRiSM.
  • Back up before clearing a device or changing the engine.

Step by step

  1. Select Historian in Live Data.
  2. No data yet? Select Start demo data 1 or Add 24 h of demo history. Refresh reloads the status.
  3. Set up live tags on the Modbus Configuration (see Chapter 6.2) page (Modbus configuration →), or tick Log form data.
  4. Under Trend, pick the range 2 and tags. Custom needs From, To, Apply range.
  5. Live follows the newest sample. Drag to pan, wheel or pinch to zoom; Reset zoom.
  6. Set Values and Layout; Export PNG.
  7. In the Data table, page with ‹ Prev / Next ›, sort by the Time heading, or Copy (tab-separated).
  8. Under Export and restore, choose format, range, tags and values, then Export 3.
  9. To restore, choose the file and Restore mode, then Restore.
  10. Under Storage and retention, set the limits and select Apply retention. A new Storage engine applies only after Switch engine (moves the data).
  11. Select Request persistent storage: else a browser may clear the data when short of space.

7 Test System Safety

7.1 ESD Hi-Pilot

Checks that the hi-pilot (PSH) shuts the well in before backflow lifts the relief device of a trapped section.

What it does

The gas held between the hi-pilot and the relief setting, divided by the backflow rate, is the time to relief. It must exceed the ESD response. Ideal gas: a screening check.

When to use it

  • Setting a hi-pilot on the choke manifold, heater or separator inlet.
  • After a change of section, relief device or ESD system.

Step by step

  1. Select ESD Pilots in Test System Safety, then ESD Hi-Pilot.
  2. Choose the Pre-set Location 1; every value stays editable.
  3. Enter the Gas Backflow Rate and check the Hi-Pilot Setting, relief setting and Section MAWP.
  4. Enter the ESD Response Time: pilot trip to valve closed.
  5. Select Calculate and read the verdict, the tables, the rationale and the notes.
  6. Reset to Preset puts back the location values.

Inputs

InputDefaultWhat to enter
Pre-set LocationDirect Steam Heater Shell
Section Volume292 ft³ (8.27 m³)
Section Gas Temp23 °F (-5 °C)
Gas Backflow Rate39.28 MMSCFD (1112 10³ m³/d)Worst case.
Gas Specific Gravity0.78Not used in the time.
Hi-Pilot Setting112 psig (772 kPa(g))At least 10 % below the MAWP.
Rupture Disc / RV Setting125 psig (862 kPa(g))At or below the MAWP.
Section MAWP125 psig (862 kPa(g))
ESD Response Time5 s

Results and verdicts

ResultMeaning
Computed ResultsTime to relief, gas vented, margin.
RationaleWhat would pass.
NotesCautions on the set points and inputs.
  • ✓ The ESD closes before the relief setting is reached. Keep the set points and response time.
  • ✗ The relief device lifts first. Lower the hi-pilot to the value in the rationale, or shorten the ESD response.

Worked example

The default inputs

  • Heater shell: 292 ft³ (8.27 m³) at 23 °F (-5 °C), backflow 39.28 MMSCFD (1112 10³ m³/d), hi-pilot 112 psig (772 kPa(g)), RV and MAWP 125 psig (862 kPa(g)), ESD 5 s.

Result:

  • ✗ FAIL: relief in 0.61 s, 2273 scf (64.4 Sm³) vented. A pass needs 19 psig (131 kPa(g)) or less.

In Metric mode the page shows the same values converted; the calculation is the same.

Tips and pitfalls

Pitfalls

  • No Z-factor: treat a small margin as a fail.
  • Act on each caution in the notes. A hi-pilot less than 10 % below the MAWP or within 5 psi (34.5 kPa) of the RV is flagged. So are an RV above the MAWP, gas below -40 °F (-40 °C) and a gas SG outside 0.55–1.20.

Standards and references

  • ASME BPVC VIII-1 UG-134; API 520 Part I — relief set pressure
  • API RP 14C — safety devices

Related modules

ESD Lo-Pilot (see Chapter 7.2) · PRV / Relief Sizing (see Chapter 9.4) · Liquid Line / RO (see Chapter 7.5)

Reviewed for v3.3.2

7.2 ESD Lo-Pilot

Checks that the lo-pilot (PSL) set point trips the ESD on a target leak in time, without false trips.

What it does

A leak lowers the section pressure steadily. The PSL must sit the false-trip margin below the flowing pressure and be reached in time.

When to use it

  • Setting a lo-pilot.
  • Checking that a small leak is seen.

Step by step

  1. Select ESD Pilots in Test System Safety, then ESD Lo-Pilot.
  2. Choose the Lo-Pilot Location 1. Custom… keeps what you type.
  3. Enter the Detectable Leak Rate 2 and the Required Detection Time.
  4. Set the False-Trip Margin below P_flow. Leave PSL Set Point to Check blank for the recommended value.
  5. Select Calculate and read the Status card.
  6. Reset Defaults puts every field back.

Inputs

InputDefaultWhat to enter
Lo-Pilot LocationUpstream of Heater Choke
Section Volume662 ft³ (18.7 m³)
Section Flowing Pressure662 psig (4564 kPa(g))
Detectable Leak Rate25 MMSCFD (708 10³ m³/d)
Section Gas Temperature60 °F (15.6 °C)
WHSIP2100 psig (14479 kPa(g))Reference only.
Required Detection Time5 s
False-Trip Margin below P_flow5 psi (34.5 kPa)
PSL Set Point to CheckBlank: flowing pressure less the margin.

Results and verdicts

ResultMeaning
PSL SettingRecommended set point and trip window.
  • ✓ The PSL trips in time. Use the recommended set point.
  • ⚠ The drop is under 2 psi (13.8 kPa), close to gauge noise. Check that the pilot can resolve it.
  • ✗ Normal swings would trip the ESD. Lower the set point to the value shown.
  • ✗ This PSL never trips. Raise it above 0 psig (0 kPa(g)).
  • ✗ The leak is seen too late. Put the PSL nearer the leak, reduce the margin or detect the rate of change.

Worked example

The default inputs

  • Heater choke: 662 ft³ (18.7 m³) at 662 psig (4564 kPa(g)), leak 25 MMSCFD (708 10³ m³/d), 5 s, margin 5 psi (34.5 kPa), PSL blank.

Result:

  • A drop of 32.1 psi (221.3 kPa) in 5 s. ✓ PASS: the PSL of 657 psig (4530 kPa(g)) trips after 0.78 s.

In Metric mode the page shows the same values converted; the calculation is the same.

Tips and pitfalls

Pitfalls

  • A real drawdown is slower: allow margin on the time.

Standards and references

  • API RP 14C — PSL set points
  • API RP 521 — depressuring

7.3 Hydrate Management

Hydrate temperature at four points of the spread, and the methanol or glycol rate that keeps each out of hydrates.

What it does

Each card finds the hydrate temperature at its downstream pressure, then the inhibitor rate (Hammerschmidt) that puts it a margin below the target.

When to use it

  • Will the choke form hydrates?
  • A quick inhibitor rate.

Step by step

  1. Select Hydrate Management in Test System Safety.
  2. In System Inputs, choose the Inhibitor, enter the Free-water rate and Gas SG.
  3. On each segment card, enter the pressures, temperatures and Operating-T target.
  4. Select Recompute all nodes. Each card shows a risk badge.
  5. A Local injection rate of 0 is replaced by the recommended rate when you select Recompute all nodes; a value you type is kept.
  6. Read the Inhibitor Injection Summary 1.

7.4 Chemical Injection

Plans hydrate inhibitor, H2S scavenger and treating-chemical injection per point, with pump settings and checks.

What it does

The page checks the spread for hydrates and designs the inhibitor for the coldest point each line protects; other chemicals use ppm doses. Each line gets a rate, pump setting and pressure.

When to use it

  • Hydrates, H2S or treating chemicals.
  • Setting injection pumps.

Step by step

  1. Select Chemical Injection in Test System Safety.
  2. Fill in Well stream 1 and Spread conditions, with the SITHP (see Appendix B) and FWHP (see Appendix B).
  3. Check the hydrate margin and J-T factor in Design basis.
  4. Choose the Number of injection lines; on each card choose the Injection point, Chemical and Pump type.
  5. Read the headline 2, then the Spread hydrate check.
  6. Read Pump setting and Discharge pressure; compare Pump options. Act on each ⚠ and ✗ line.
  7. Calibrate in Field calibration check.
  8. Select an ⓘ or a topic in Background and standards for the background, cautions and standards.

7.5 Liquid Line / RO

Gas blowby through a failed-open separator dump valve: is a restrictive orifice needed, and does it protect the tank?

What it does

If the level control valve (LCV) fails open, gas blows by to the tank. The page compares it with the vent capacity and checks the restrictive orifice (RO).

When to use it

  4. Select Calculate and read RO Required? and RO Adequacy 2.
  5. Keep ignition out of the Lean Flammability Footprint.

  5. Select Calculate or change a value; read the verdicts 2.

8 Separation & Process

8.1 Separator Retention

Estimates how long liquid stays in the separator from its capacity, the liquid level and the flow rate.

What it does

Retention time is the liquid held divided by the liquid rate. On a horizontal vessel a gauge reads height; the page can turn a level in % of the ID into % of volume.

When to use it

  • Before a test, at the expected liquid rate.
  • When the rate or the level set point changes.

Step by step

  1. Select Separators in Separation & Process, then Separator Retention.
  2. Enter the Separator Capacity 1 and the Fluid Level 2; choose the Level Basis 3.
  3. Enter the liquid Flow Rate 4: oil plus water.
  4. Select Calculate. Read the time and status; compare them with the Guidelines.

Inputs

InputDefaultWhat to enter
Separator Capacity17.4 bbl (2.77 m³)
Fluid Level50 %
Level Basis% of ID height for a gauge on a horizontal vessel.
Flow Rate6600 BPD (1049 m³/d)

Results and verdicts

ResultMeaning
Retention TimeIn mm:ss and minutes.
StatusADEQUATE from 3 minutes, LOW from 1, CRITICALLY LOW below: raise the level or cut the rate.

Worked example

The default inputs

  • 17.4 bbl (2.77 m³) at 50 %, 6600 BPD (1049 m³/d).

Result:

  • 8.7 bbl (1.4 m³) held; 1.9 minutes: LOW — May be insufficient.

In Metric mode the page shows the same values converted; the calculation is the same.

Tips and pitfalls

Tips

  • More level or less rate gives more time; then check the gas on Separator Rating (see Chapter 8.2).

Pitfalls

  • A 25 % level by height is 19.6 % of a horizontal vessel.

Standards and references

  • API Spec 12J — oil and gas separators

8.2 Separator Rating

Rates a separator: Souders-Brown gas capacity and liquid retention against a target, with one PASS or FAIL.

What it does

K follows the orientation and foaming. Gas flows above the liquid in a horizontal vessel, through the full bore in a vertical one. Water is added from the BS&W (see Appendix B). The retention target is 3, 5 or 10 minutes for low, medium or high foaming. Z is taken as 0.9.

When to use it

  • Before a test, at the expected gas and oil rates.
  • When the rates rise or the fluid foams.

Step by step

  1. Select Separators in Separation & Process, then Separator Rating.
  2. Enter Separator Details 1 and Fluid Data.
  3. Set the Foaming Tendency: it sets K and the target.
  4. Select Calculate. Read PASS or FAIL, then any red row.

8.3 Separator Handling

Screens a separator and its outlets: gas capacity, retention, slug volume, outlet velocities and valve Cv.

What it does

K is ×1.5 with a mesh pad; retention is split between oil and water by the BS&W (see Appendix B). Each outlet valve, line and bore is checked against your limit and the API RP 14E erosional velocity.

Temperature is in degrees Celsius and the limits in m/s on both unit settings.

When to use it

  • Before rig-up: check the vessel, valve and line sizes.

  2. Fill Configuration 1, Operating Conditions and Fluids.
  3. Enter the outlet sizes; 0 = no orifice fitting or turbine.
  4. Check Velocity & Cv Limits, then select Calculate.
  5. Read the verdict 2 and each ✗ and ⚠ line; apply the Recommendation lines.

11 Well Test Simulator

11.1 Well Test Simulator

A live replay of a well test spread around a steady design calculation: line-ups, levels, alarms, ESD, tank gauging, upsets.

What it does

The form feeds a steady calculation from the wellhead through the choke, back-walked from the separator Operating Pressure. The live view runs it in time. Training: course (see Chapter 11) and scenarios (see Chapter 12).

When to use it

  • Train a crew before a job.
  • Check a line-up: where gas and liquids go.
  • Practise upsets: dump valve failure, ESD, hydrates, tank overfill.

Step by step

  1. Select Well Test Simulator in Well Test & Flowlines: the live view 1 opens.
  2. Enter the data in Well Parameters, Choke, Heater and Separator.
  3. Set the line-up in the Rig-up card 2.
  4. Run the test from the toolbar 3: play, speed, Reset.
  5. Read the HUD. Select equipment for its card.
  6. Answer alarms in the alarm bar and the Alarms drawer.
  7. Check the steady results: Node Conditions, Pipe Segment Analysis.

Worked example

The default spread (steady check)

  • WHP (see Appendix B) 3000 psig (20684 kPa(g)); 10 MMSCFD (283 10³ m³/d), 1000 BPD (159 m³/d) oil, 200 BPD (31.8 m³/d) water; bean (see Appendix B) 32/64; separator 150 psig (1034 kPa(g)).

Result:

  • Choke downstream 157.7 psig (1087.3 kPa(g)), P2/P1 0.057: Critical.
  • Maximum rate at this ratio 10.71 MMSCFD (303.27 10³ m³/d): no flow limit. Fired duty 2.103 MMBtu/hr (616.328 kW).

In Metric mode the page shows the same values converted; the calculation is the same.

Tips and pitfalls

Tips

  • Use 2D on a projector or an older device.
  • Form and rig-up changes apply live and are logged in Events.

Pitfalls

  • It does not predict what a well makes on a bean: the rates are inputs.

Standards and references

  • API RP 14E — erosional velocity, C-factor

Related modules

Dual Choke (see Chapter 3.3) · Choke Performance & Critical Flow (see Chapter 3.6) · Multiphase Flowline Pressure Drop (see Chapter 4.3) · Hydrate Management (see Chapter 7.3) · Separator Retention (see Chapter 8.1) · Flare Simulation (see Chapter 9.1)

Key idea

What it does

The bean is checked against the gas rate only: too small, and all three rates are cut by the same factor and CK-101 raises CHOKE_LIMIT.

Page layout

What it does

Top: the live view (toolbar, alarm bar, view, HUD) and the Rig-up card; below: the form cards, Pipe Segments, API RP 14E Settings, results.

Form inputs

What it does

A production line: Operating Pressure plus the line loss through V-101, or Production line pressure with V-101 out (FS-2 (see Chapter 12)). Burner boom: FS-1 (see Chapter 12).
